Diagnose Variable Label Consistency

Source: R/label_consistency.R
label_consistency.Rd

Produces a descriptive, tidy report of label-consistency problems in variable metadata. Unlike assess_label_quality() (indicator U-001), this function does not score or emit R4SUB evidence rows; it is a diagnostic aid that surfaces three classes of finding:

Usage

label_consistency(metadata)

Arguments

metadata

A data frame with at least columns dataset (character), variable (character), and label (character). An optional table_label column (character) supplies the dataset-level label used for the missing_table_label check.

Value

A tibble with one row per finding and the columns:

finding_type

One of "duplicate_label", "inconsistent_label", or "missing_table_label".

dataset

The dataset the finding relates to.

variable

The variable the finding relates to, or NA for a dataset-level finding.

label

The variable label involved, or NA where not applicable.

detail

A human-readable description of the finding.

When there are no findings, a zero-row tibble with the same columns is returned.

Details

duplicate_label

Two or more variables in the same dataset share an identical (non-empty) label.

inconsistent_label

A variable name that appears in more than one dataset carries different labels across those datasets.

missing_table_label

A dataset has no dataset-level (table) label. Only checked when a table_label column is supplied.

Comparisons ignore leading and trailing white space. Empty strings and NA are treated as missing labels and never counted as duplicates or inconsistencies.

See also

assess_label_quality() for the scored U-001 indicator.

Examples

meta <- data.frame(
  dataset  = c("ADSL", "ADSL", "ADAE", "ADAE"),
  variable = c("USUBJID", "SUBJID", "USUBJID", "AETERM"),
  label    = c("Subject ID", "Subject ID",
               "Unique Subject Identifier", "Reported Term"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
label_consistency(meta)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   finding_type       dataset variable label                     detail          
#>   <chr>              <chr>   <chr>    <chr>                     <chr>           
#> 1 duplicate_label    ADSL    SUBJID   Subject ID                label 'Subject …
#> 2 duplicate_label    ADSL    USUBJID  Subject ID                label 'Subject …
#> 3 inconsistent_label ADAE    USUBJID  Unique Subject Identifier variable 'USUBJ…
#> 4 inconsistent_label ADSL    USUBJID  Subject ID                variable 'USUBJ…

# With a dataset-level (table) label column
meta2 <- data.frame(
  dataset     = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),
  variable    = c("USUBJID", "USUBJID"),
  label       = c("Unique Subject Identifier", "Unique Subject Identifier"),
  table_label = c("Subject-Level Analysis Dataset", ""),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
label_consistency(meta2)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   finding_type        dataset variable label detail                             
#>   <chr>               <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>                              
#> 1 missing_table_label ADAE    NA       NA    dataset 'ADAE' has no dataset-leve…
